evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for polling triggers; a developer's own app can use shorter intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still [white-label the Connect Link page](/docs/authentication/white-labeling-authentication#customizing-the-connect-link) with your logo and app title without needing your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Even without a custom OAuth app, a developer can white-label the Connect Link page with their logo and app title.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: A custom auth config lets the developer supply their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials for a toolkit (this describes custom auth configs generally, not Gmail specifically).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest.
evidence.answer: A developer can mix approaches: their own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (named as GitHub, Google, Slack), and managed auth for the rest; each toolkit has its own auth config.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: The process took me almost 3 full months to complete.
evidence.answer: One developer's OAuth consent-screen verification took almost 3 months, with four rounds of feedback mostly about privacy policy, branding and demo video (a single developer report, not an official timeline).

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Ten-plus rejections. No emails for any of them.
evidence.answer: An agency developer reported more than ten rejections over about two months, several with no notification email, so the status had to be checked manually in the verification centre.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Checking your demo video, we noticed a discrepancy between the scopes in your Cloud Console and the scopes to which your application is making API calls.
evidence.answer: A common blocker reported was a mismatch between the scopes listed in the Cloud Console and the scopes the app actually calls, which led to rejection.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: The Google verification and security assessment processes can take several weeks or longer
evidence.answer: A third-party provider guide (Nylas) says Google verification plus the security assessment for restricted Gmail scopes can take several weeks or longer.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Gmail scopes that read or modify mail are restricted, and restricted scopes trigger OAuth verification plus a Cloud App Security Assessment (CASA) for any app that handles the data on its servers.
evidence.answer: Gmail read/modify scopes are restricted and require both OAuth verification and a CASA security assessment if the app stores or transmits data on its servers.
